metadata.title: The first three seconds: writing an opening that keeps viewers

scenes.voiceText: Viewers decide whether to stay or scroll within the first few seconds. However good the rest is, it means nothing if nobody gets there. Here is how to write an opening that holds them.

inputs.punchline: Here is how to write an opening that holds them

scenes.voiceText: Open the analytics of any video and you will see a funnel. Most viewers drop out right at the start. That is why fixing the first three seconds usually pays off more than fixing anything after it.
A suggested shape for a thirty-second video. Three seconds of opening, seven for the problem, fifteen for the fix, five for the call to action. The shortest part is the one that matters most.

inputs.title: How to split a 30-second video
inputs.source: A suggested structure — adjust to your content

scenes.voiceText: Two kinds of opening. The weak one: a greeting, an introduction, a logo. The strong one goes straight in: say the result now, ask what the viewer is already wondering, or show something unexpected.

inputs.title: Weak opening vs strong opening
inputs.left_1: Hi everyone, today I'm going to...
inputs.right_1: Say the result viewers want, now
inputs.right_2: The question they are asking themselves
inputs.right_3: An unexpected image in the first frame
inputs.verdict: Go straight to what viewers care about

scenes.voiceText: The easiest formula: give the result first, explain how after. Instead of today I'll show you how to bake a cake, say this cake needs only three ingredients. Viewers stay to find out how.

inputs.caption: The easiest opening formula to use

scenes.voiceText: Everyone who makes videos has done this. Spend the first five seconds saying hello, then wonder why nobody watches to the end. Viewers don't dislike you, they just haven't seen a reason to stay.

inputs.kicker: Every video maker has done it
inputs.caption: Five seconds of hello, then wondering why nobody watches to the end

scenes.voiceText: There are many kinds of opening, but if you are starting out, try a question that hits the viewer's pain point. It is easy, just one sentence, and it makes people want the answer.

inputs.card_title: A question that hits the pain
inputs.feature_1: Just one sentence, no extra footage needed
inputs.feature_2: Viewers see themselves in the question
inputs.feature_3: Example: Are you wasting your first 5 seconds?
inputs.takeaway: A question that hits the viewer's pain point is easy to write and sparks curiosity, so it is the first one worth trying.

scenes.voiceText: And you, why do you usually scroll past a video? A long-winded opening, or an overblown title with nothing behind it? Your answer is what your own viewers are thinking too.

inputs.question: Why do you scroll past a video?
inputs.cta: Tell us your reason in the comments

scenes.voiceText: Today's exercise: take your latest video and rewrite only the opening line, keep everything else. Post the new version and compare how many viewers stay past three seconds. The numbers will answer for you.

inputs.desc: Rewrite only the opening line of your latest video, repost, compare viewers past 3s.

scenes.voiceText: Follow the channel for more opening formulas for every industry.
